title: James McAvoy says he ‘nearly died’ after his lungs collapsed following botched biopsy
summary: James McAvoy revealed how a "botched" lung biopsy nearly killed him and led to weeks in the hospital before he underwent an intense physical transformation for his "Glass" role.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
James McAvoy opened up about a life-threatening health scare that left him hospitalized for several weeks after what he described as a botched medical procedure.

During a recent appearance on Dax Shepard's "Armchair Expert" podcast, the 47-year-old actor recalled how he pushed his body to its limits for his transformation into the Beast in 2019's "Glass" after first recovering from a serious infection and collapsed lungs.
"I'd actually been in hospital and I had a lung puncture because… they saw a shadow in my lung, so they wanted to biopsy it to see if it was cancer, which it wasn't, which was great," McAvoy said.
"But that was botched, and I nearly died," he continued. "I was at home two days later and my lungs just collapsed in bed one night, and I was on my own as well, so it was crazy."
SHARON STONE CLAIMS EX-HUSBAND SIGNED HER UP FOR BRAIN SURGERY WITHOUT HER CONSENT AFTER STROKE
James McAvoy said a botched lung biopsy nearly killed him.  (Getty Images for IMDb)
The "X-Men: First Class" star said he spent two or three weeks in the hospital while doctors worked unsuccessfully to clear his lungs.

"They tried everything to clean out," McAvoy recalled. "Nothing was working. So, they were like, 'We're going to need to cut you open big-style. Go in with like soapy, like dish soap basically, and just like clean you out, scoop it all out.'"
McAvoy said his lungs collapsed while he was alone in bed. (Dave Benett/WireImage)

McAvoy recalled that after his medical ordeal, he underwent an intense process for the next four or five months as he bulked up to reprise his role in "Glass." In the M. Night Shyamalan-directed movie, the actor portrayed Kevin Wendell Crumb, who suffers from severe dissociative identity disorder (DID) with 24 distinct personalities.
MATT DAMON REFUSES TO PUT BODY IN 'DANGEROUS' SITUATIONS FOR HOLLYWOOD ROLES AFTER TURNING 50

McAvoy first played Wendell in 2016's "Split," which was the sequel to 2000's "Unbreakable." In "Split," Wendell's 24th personality "The Beast," who possesses superhuman strength, speed, durability and pain suppression, became the central threat after emerging toward the end of the film.
"Unlike ‘Split,’ I was the Beast, like most of the movie," McAvoy recalled. "So I was like, 'I'm really going to need to do the real thing. I'm going to need to go for it.'"
'THE ODYSSEY' STAR MATT DAMON REVEALS BRUTAL SIX-MONTH TRANSFORMATION BEHIND CHRISTOPHER NOLAN FILM
"I remember saying to [Shyamalan] like, ‘You’re going to need to get me a trainer,'" he said.
The "Split" star said he spent weeks in the hospital before undergoing an intense physical transformation for his role in "Glass."  (Getty Images)
McAvoy explained that Shyamalan offered to hire a trainer from "the local gym," but he rejected that idea.
'SUITS' STAR RICK HOFFMAN REVEALS 'INTENSE' ROUTINE BEHIND DRAMATIC PHYSICAL TRANSFORMATION
McAvoy said he had worked with trainers from local gyms before but needed someone who could transform his physique into that of a figure from Greek mythology.
"The guy that worked with me was amazing," he added. "He didn't move in with me, but he was just with me a lot and kind of regulated what I ate and trained me just right."
SYLVESTER STALLONE REVEALS SURPRISING HEALTH STRUGGLE BEHIND HIS FAMOUSLY RIPPED PHYSIQUE

"For the first four weeks, he rehabilitated me. I could walk, but I couldn’t run, couldn’t cycle, couldn’t jog," McAvoy recalled. "So he did a lot of rehabilitation and, sort of, functional movement, and then put the pounds on me really fast."
McAvoy said he couldn't run or jog at the beginning of his training. (Getty Images for IMDb)
McAvoy recently claimed that he was bullied on the set of the hit HBO miniseries "Band of Brothers."
'BLIND SIDE' STAR QUINTON AARON SAYS HE 'SAW JESUS' WHILE IN A COMA AFTER NEAR-FATAL STROKE

While recently appearing on "Watch What Happens Live with Andy Cohen," McAvoy was asked to rate his experience working on different projects, and when he was shown a picture of the show's cast, he recalled that one of his co-stars organized a group to mock him on set.

"On my first day on set, there was a ton of actors," he began. "It was one of those scenes with everybody in it, and we’re all at a bar, and I had a scene. And all these guys were in it for nine months, 10 months, and they get one line in one episode, and one line 10 episodes later. They were all pissed. I come in for one episode, and I’ve got an arc and scenes. I’ve got tons of lines."
SHARON STONE SAYS SHE 'NEARLY DIED' AFTER 'BASIC INSTINCT' OPENED THE DOOR TO HOLLYWOOD'S DARK SIDE
When the photo, which featured many of his co-stars from the show, flashed on the screen, McAvoy confirmed that a specific actor was in the photo.
The actor recently claimed that he was bullied on the set of "Band of Brothers." (Getty Images)

"So, one of the guys in that picture decided to bully me on my first day as a professional actor out of acting school," he said. "He got him and his buddies to just stand pointing at me and laugh at me for like three minutes."
While he didn't name names, the photo featured Donnie Wahlberg, Kirk Acevedo, Scott Grimes, Neal McDonough, Adam James, Frank John Hughes, Philip Barantini and Ross McCall.
McAvoy added that not everyone on set participated in the bullying, saying Dexter Fletcher and Robin Laing "took me aside, and they were like, ‘Come hang with us, man.'"

title: Cindy Crawford mourns son Presley Gerber in heartbreaking tribute
summary: Cindy Crawford called Presley Gerber a "sweet, beautiful soul" in an emotional Instagram tribute weeks after his death at a rehabilitation facility.
story: Presley Gerber, model and son of Cindy Crawford, has died at the age of 27 in a Los Angeles rehab facility. TMZ executive producer Michael Babcock joins 'America's Newsroom' to discuss the ongoing investigation into Gerber's death as a suspected overdose. The tragedy follows Gerber's previous public statements regarding his mental health and substance abuse struggles.
Cindy Crawford, Rande Gerber and Kaia Gerber are remembering their late son and brother, Presley Walker Gerber, as a "sweet, beautiful soul" in heartbreaking tributes shared weeks after his death.
"Presley Walker Gerber. July 2, 1999—September 20, 2026," Crawford wrote on Instagram, alongside a photo of her son.

"We are beyond heartbroken to lose our beloved son and brother. We feel so blessed to have had Presley in our lives for 27 years," she continued. "He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever."
Crawford praised Presley for "how he showed up in the world, with kindness and vulnerability" and thanked the public for supporting the family since the devastating loss.
GEORGE CLOONEY SAYS FAMILY IS STILL PROCESSING PRESLEY GERBER'S TRAGIC DEATH
Presley Gerber died Sept. 20. He was 27.  (WWD via Getty Images)

"We are grateful for the outpouring of love and support from so many who know and love our family and even strangers who feel our pain," the model wrote. "Til we meet again our sweet boy. We love you forever, Mom, Dad and Kaia."
PRESLEY GERBER DEAD AT 27: WHAT TO KNOW ABOUT CINDY CRAWFORD, RANDE GERBER'S FAMILY
Kaia, Presley’s younger sister, shared her own tribute on Instagram, describing her brother as her "ultimate teacher," "best buddy" and "great protector."
Presley Gerber was the only son of Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber. (Alberto Rodriguez/Variety via Getty Images)
CHAD LOWE’S DAUGHTER MABEL SHARES HEARTBREAKING TRIBUTE TO LATE SISTER FIONA, 13
"I don’t have the words," Kaia wrote. "And maybe the tiny mercy is that we didn’t need them all along. Words fail and words subtract and words summarize and words always lack truth."

"You know how much i loved being your sister: it has always been, and will forever be, my favorite thing about myself. i came into this world with a white-knuckle grip around you. i had more love for you than i knew what to do with. and now that it has nowhere obvious to go, i’m certain it’s going to swallow me whole."
"you believed — always believed — in people. you met cruelty not with anger, but with confusion. and curiosity. you believed people were inherently good because, presley, you are inherently good."
Kaia recalled being scared to get her ears pierced when the two were younger.
"i got scared before getting my ears pierced, so you went first. you always went first. but when i held the earring they took from your body, all i could think was: that belongs to you."
Rande Gerber, Kaia Gerber, Cindy Crawford and Presley Gerber attend The Fashion Awards 2018 in partnership with Swarovski at Royal Albert Hall on Dec. 10, 2018, in London, England. (Getty Images)
"and i really f—ing wish you hadn’t gone first this time."
In another passage, Kaia said she was still learning how to be Presley’s sister "in a world that I can’t reach for you in."
"I don’t know how to do that yet," she wrote.
She ended the tribute with a series of heartbreaking declarations.
"My darling brother. I do adore you," Kaia wrote. "I love my brother. My brother is dead."
"And this party sucks so bad without you, prez," she added.
Gerber died Sept. 20 at age 27 while staying at a rehabilitation facility, according to records from the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner.
Presley Gerber, Cindy Crawford's son, died Sept. 20, 2026. He was 27. (Paul Archuleta)
PRESLEY GERBER’S FINAL HOURS AT REHAB IN FOCUS AMID CAUSE OF DEATH QUESTIONS
The model's cause of death was "deferred," according to online records from the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner.
The medical examiner told Fox News Digital that "the investigation is still ongoing and there is limited information available."
PRESLEY GERBER’S DEATH SPARKS QUESTIONS ABOUT OVERDOSE, WITHDRAWAL AND REHAB SAFETY
Santa Monica Police Department officials are investigating the death as "a suspected overdose," according to a release from the department.
A representative for the family told Fox News Digital, "The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time."
GEORGE CLOONEY RUSHES TO RANDE GERBER AND CINDY CRAWFORD'S SIDE AFTER SON PRESLEY'S DEATH
Months before his death, Presley Gerber shared a raw look at his battle with addiction and the treatment he hoped would help him find his way back to himself.
In March, the model posted a video of himself preparing to undergo an "ibogaine flood dose," a psychedelic treatment, at a wellness clinic in Cancún, Mexico.

According to Stanford Medicine, ibogaine is a naturally occurring psychedelic derived from the root bark of the Tabernanthe iboga shrub. It has "gained interest from the medical and scientific communities for its potential to treat opioid and cocaine addiction, and research has suggested that it increases signaling of several important molecules within the brain, some of which have been linked to drug addiction and depression."

Kaia Gerber, Rande Gerber, model Cindy Crawford and Presley Gerber attend Rock4EB! 2015 with Ed Sheeran and David Spade on Nov. 15, 2015, in Malibu, California. (Todd Williamson/Getty Images for EB Kids)
The treatment is legal in some countries, but not in the United States.
"Quiet moment before everything changed," Presley Gerber wrote in the Instagram caption. "I was absolutely terrified, and I knew I would be again if I ever had to face something like this."
Gerber said letting go of control was difficult, but he trusted "there was something bigger than me guiding it."
CARA DELEVINGNE ADMITS SHE USED PARTY DRUG GHB DAILY BEFORE TERRIFYING SEIZURES FORCED HER SOBER
"I knew why I was there. I faced what I had been running from, and somewhere in all of it, I started finding my way back to myself," he wrote.
He also said he was "praying it’s the last time" he would need to return for treatment.

Presley Gerber’s post was one of several instances in which he publicly documented his recovery journey. In recent years, he had spoken candidly about depression, panic attacks, addiction and the challenges of seeking treatment.
During a 2023 episode of the "Studio 22" podcast, Presley Gerber discussed his experiences with depression and other mental health challenges.
Rande Gerber, Cindy Crawford and Presley Walker Gerber attend Chanel Dinner Celebrating our Majestic Oceans, A Benefit for NRDC on June 2, 2018, in Malibu, California.  (Stefanie Keenan/WireImage)
"[Mental health] is an issue. It is such a big part of my life. It’s a 24/7 job, and there’s so much to it," he said.

"That’s really what I want to do is help people, whether you’re depressed, you’re struggling with something that is having a negative effect on your body," he continued. "I mean it could be anything, and there’s no judgment."
Gerber said he hoped his experiences could help other people avoid making similar mistakes.

"I’ve seen a lot of stuff, and I’ve learned a lot of things," he said. "What I hope I can do is have made the mistakes for some other people, so they don’t have to make the same mistakes that I made."
He also explained why he wanted to be open about his mental health journey.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Having struggled with mental health, depression and some other things that come along with that, I think that whether I help one person or a hundred people get out of that place that I was in at one point in my life, that’s all I need to do," Gerber said.

title: Courteney Cox shows off beach body in black bikini during recent trip to Hawaii
summary: Courteney Cox stunned in a black bikini during a Hawaii beach outing, and photos capture the 62-year-old's fit physique in the tropical surf.
story: Courteney Cox explained growing up in Alabama, she never thought getting a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame would be possible, but she is so honored to receive one.
Courteney Cox proves age is just a number.
During a recent trip to Hawaii to celebrate her friend, Jennifer Meyer's wedding, the 62-year-old actress was spotted enjoying a day at the beach.
The "Cougar Town" star was photographed smiling in a black bikini while standing on the beach.

She paired the bikini with layered gold necklaces and earrings, and wore her hair in a ponytail to take a dip in the ocean. In the photos, she is seen standing knee-deep in the water before wrapping a towel over her body to dry off.
Cox was photographed in a black bikini while at the beach in Hawaii. (Backgrid)
PAULINA PORIZKOVA, HALLE BERRY AND ELIZABETH HURLEY PROVE AGE IS JUST A NUMBER IN BIKINI PHOTOS

Cox has shared how she manages to stay fit as she gets older, telling Marie Claire in September 2022 that she takes vitamins in the mornings, in addition to drinking "the cucumber, pineapple, ginger, and lemon thing."

"I play tennis twice a week. I used to box twice a week, but my left knee is hurt," she said about her fitness routine. "I also do pilates once a week. As I get older, I realize it's more important for me to do weights. It’s amazing how I used to be really muscley but not so much anymore."
She later gave fans a glimpse of her workout routine in an Instagram video in July 2024, which showed her running on a treadmill, pull-ups, squats and crunches.

The "Friends" star was also seen enjoying her summer while on a luxury yacht off the Spanish island of Mallorca with her longtime friend, Jennifer Aniston, and other actors, including Judd Apatow, Leslie Mann and Pedro Pascal.

Following Perry's death in October 2023, Cox shared on "CBS Sunday Morning," that Perry was "probably one of the funniest human beings in the world."
"I’m so thankful I got to work so closely with him for so many years," she said. "He visits me a lot, if we believe in that."

title: Val Chmerkovskiy suspended from 'Dancing With the Stars' over Will Smith Oscars slap reference
summary: Val Chmerkovskiy's since-deleted TikTok appeared to reference Will Smith's Oscar slap after Carrie Ann Inaba criticized wife Jenna Johnson's routine.
story: The "Dancing with the Stars" co-host spoke with Fox News Digital as she walked the Emmy Awards red carpet.

Val Chmerkovskiy has been suspended from "Dancing With the Stars" after appearing to reference Will Smith’s infamous Oscars slap in a since-deleted social media post defending his wife, fellow pro dancer Jenna Johnson.
The professional dancer, 40, will miss Tuesday’s "Dedication Night" episode, marking the first known suspension of a professional dancer in the show’s history, according to ABC.
BBC Studios, which produces the ABC dance competition, confirmed the disciplinary action on Saturday.
Val Chmerkovskiy has been suspended from "DWTS" after a controversial comment made against judge Carrie Ann Inaba. (Getty Images)

"The well-being of everyone who works on ‘Dancing with the Stars’ is non-negotiable," the company said in a statement. "Val’s social media post was inappropriate and does not reflect the values or standards expected of anyone connected with the show. As a result, he will not participate in next week’s show."

The controversy began after Carrie Ann Inaba criticized Johnson and her celebrity dance partner, actor Harry Shum Jr., during "Super Bowl Night" last week. Inaba called out a lift in the couple’s samba routine and even read the definition of a lift during her critique.

Val, who is married to Johnson, appeared to defend her in a TikTok post that read, "You almost saw the Fresh Prince enter the ballroom last night." The comment was widely viewed as a reference to Smith slapping comedian Chris Rock during the 2022 Academy Awards.

Judges Carrie Ann Inaba, Derek Hough, Bruno Tonioli and Alfonso Ribeiro, along with pro dancer Jenna Johnson and contestant Harry Shum Jr., appear during "Mariah Carey Night" on Dancing With the Stars. (Disney via Getty Images)
The post was later deleted, and Val apologized to Inaba publicly and privately.

"In a moment where my instinct was to defend my wife, I made a poor decision to reference a meme to ‘keep my wife’s name’ out of the conversation, without stopping to think through what else that reference could imply, which was genuinely never my intention," he wrote on his Instagram Stories.
"Carrie Ann certainly didn’t deserve to get caught in the middle of my bad judgment, and I hate that she was," he added.
Val also said he did not want the controversy to overshadow the upcoming episode or distract from his celebrity partner, Jenna Dewan.
"DWTS" judge Carrie Ann Inaba once admitted to being harder on the female contestants. (Getty Images)

"The last thing I want is to become a distraction from an important week or from the incredible work my dance partner Jenna Dewan is putting in," he wrote. "Please send Carrie Ann, Jenna, and the whole ‘DWTS’ family lots of love during Dedication Night. I’ll be watching and cheering everyone on!!"

title: Jana Kramer says Los Angeles priced her out of the childhood she wanted for her kids
summary: Jana Kramer reveals why she left Studio City for Nashville, giving her kids the Midwest-style childhood she cherished while growing up in Michigan.
story: The actress admitted to Fox News Digital she couldn't afford to give her kids the childhood she wanted for them when living in Los Angeles.
Jana Kramer is opening up about not being able to afford to give her children the life she wanted for them.

During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 42-year-old actress spoke about her new film, "The One," and how moving to Nashville, Tennessee has allowed her to give her kids the childhood she had.

"I remember being in Studio City with the two kids, and we couldn't afford to have a bigger place with a bigger backyard and neighborhoods like that. Again, we just couldn't afford certain neighborhoods and, for me, Tennessee has just always been a place that every time I land, my nervous system just like relaxes, it feels calm," she said.

As someone who grew up in the Midwest, she "struggled" with the idea that some of her "greatest memories as a child" included running around her "neighborhood and just going from friend's house to friend's house," and staying out playing "until the sun went down."
Kramer recalled not being able to afford the life she wanted to give her children when living in Los Angeles. (Jason Kempin/Getty Images)
JANA KRAMER SAYS HOLDING ON TO TOXIC RELATIONSHIPS 'DRAINS YOU' UNTIL YOU ‘START LOSING YOURSELF' COMPLETELY

After moving to Tennessee, she said it now brings her joy to watch her children having a similar childhood, spending their days "on their bikes and going to their friends houses," noting "it just makes me feel like home."
"I love it here. You can always go back," she added. "You can always go to Hollywood, but things have changed so much with self-tapes, which I actually don't love, but you can. It's a plane away."
WATCH: Jana Kramer moved to Nashville to give her kids a taste of her Midwestern childhood
The "One Tree Hill" star explained that while she knows many people who are raising their children in Los Angeles, and "that's amazing for them," she enjoys the "totally different life" in Tennessee.
She attributes her affinity towards Tennessee to her own upbringing in Michigan, noting she values how she was raised, "that I just really wanted that same upbringing for my kids."
Kramer has two sons and a daughter with her ex-husband Mike Caussin and her current husband, Alan Russell. (Tibrina Hobson/Getty Images)

The actress shares two children with her ex-husband Mike Caussin – Jolie and Jace – and a son, Roman, with her husband Allan Russell.
Kramer's latest film, "The One," tells the story of an 18-year-old navigating through homelessness after aging out of the foster care system.
Kramer stars in the upcoming movie, "The One." (Zachary Burns)

"I remember reading the script and just, I love a complicated story,  you know, I think it's always fun to play those roles because life is complex," she said. "But I loved the story behind it. I loved the faith element. It wasn't completely thrown in your face, but it was a beautiful thread throughout the movie. And it just had a lot of heart to it. And so I felt that in the movie, and then I felt that pain that everyone was going through. And so, I just really wanted to be a part of telling that story."

"The One" hits theaters nationwide on Nov 5th, coinciding with national homeless youth awareness month, bringing timely attention to the film’s story.

The new film focuses on foster care and teen homelessness.  (Zachary Burns)

The actress shared that the movie is "shedding light" on this issue, noting it was "heartbreaking" to see the character portray the feeling of "not having a home base" and living with the idea that at "any second the rug can be pulled from underneath them."

"I just… I can't imagine that as a kid," she said. "It's like I think about my kids, and it makes me sad to think about. Them not feeling safe or them being put into unsafe homes because our job as parents is to protect them. And it makes me really sad that, some kids in the foster system don't get placed into safe homes and those that have to hop around."

title: Poison drummer Rikki Rockett recorded messages for his kids as cancer threatened to take his tongue
summary: Poison drummer Rikki Rockett recorded goodbye messages for his young children after doctors discussed removing his tongue to fight throat cancer.
story: Facing the possibility of losing his tongue, Poison drummer Rikki Rockett recorded messages for his kids. Now, he's celebrating 10 years cancer-free. Rockett is the author of a new memoir, "Ghost Notes: My Life in Poison."
Poison drummer Rikki Rockett was staring down a terrifying possibility as he battled cancer: Doctors might have to remove his tongue.
After chemotherapy and radiation failed to stop the disease, the rocker began recording messages for his young children so they could remember the sound of his voice.

"I was recording pieces of information for my kids so they could watch it, because the next step was to cut my tongue out if they had to," Rockett (born Richard Allan Ream) told Fox News Digital. "And I wanted them to know what I sounded like and my advice to them growing up, and I wanted them to hear it from me. I wanted them to understand what I was, what I thought I was or would become."
HOW THE NELSON TWINS WENT FROM PACKING ARENAS TO BEING 'F---ING BROKE' DESPITE MAKING MILLIONS
Poison, from left: Bobby Dall, C.C. DeVille, Bret Michaels and Rikki Rockett, circa 1987. Rockett has written a memoir, "Ghost Notes: My Life in Poison." (Courtesy Everett Collection)
Rockett, whose weight dropped to 161 pounds during treatment, said the possibility of losing his tongue left him fearing he might not survive much longer.

"I would've most likely had a feeding tube," he said. "I don't think I would've lived much longer. It would've added another year or two. Some people do make it. Some people get all of that done and live for a long time. But I think a lot of times, with the way it was going with me, I don't think I would've survived, quite honestly."
Fox News may be compensated for or earn a commission if you buy through our referral links.
Rikki Rockett's memoir, "Ghost Notes: My Life in Poison," is available now. (Rare Bird Books)
Now 65, Rockett says he has been free of cancer for a decade. His memoir, "Ghost Notes: My Life in Poison," chronicles his rise to stardom during the decadent '80s and his grueling health battle.
WATCH: POISON DRUMMER RIKKI ROCKETT RECALLS HEARTBREAKING CANCER BATTLE
In 2015, Rockett said he and his family developed sore throats. They were all prescribed antibiotics, but while everyone else recovered, his symptoms persisted.
Rockett returned to the doctor, who examined his nose and throat with a scope. During the examination, the doctor spotted something suspicious.
Rikki Rockett of Poison performs at Oracle Arena in Oakland, California, on June 13, 2017. (Alamy Stock Photo)
"I don't know if it's cancer, but it's suspicious, and we got to do a biopsy," Rockett recalled his doctor telling him. "My life changed at that very second."
Before his cancer diagnosis, Rikki Rockett had a persistent sore throat that lasted for months. (Courtesy of Rikki Rockett)
According to the Head and Neck Cancer Alliance, Rockett was diagnosed with HPV-related throat cancer in 2015. The disease affected the base of his tongue.

According to his memoir, Rockett had experienced a sore throat and a swollen lymph node for more than a month. It hurt every time he swallowed. After doctors diagnosed him with cancer, he received radiation and chemotherapy.
Rikki Rockett attends the First Annual Concrete Foundations Awards on Oct. 3, 1991, at the Los Angeles Airport Marriott Hotel. (Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)

"Before long, I couldn't eat solid food anymore," he wrote. "My weight dropped dramatically because all I could manage was soup, shakes and water. Eventually, I couldn't eat or drink anything at all."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Rikki Rockett feared losing his tongue and time with his beloved children. (Courtesy of Rikki Rockett)

Rockett wrote: "I've got throat cancer. At its worst, I struggle to swallow even a gulp of water. This morning, my son had to watch tears running down my cheeks as I tried to eat a spoonful of soup. He looked terrified."

Rockett told Fox News Digital that he eventually "wound up in stage 4." For three months, he received radiation five days a week, along with chemotherapy weekly, but he said the treatment failed. Doctors then discussed removing his tongue, according to Rockett.
Poison drummer Rikki Rockett performs at The Wharf in Orange Beach, on July 7, 2011. (Alamy Live News)
Rockett was terrified. In his memoir, he wrote that he believed he had only a "40 or 50 percent chance of living." But he refused to give up.
From left: C.C. DeVille, Bret Michaels, Rikki Rockett, and Bobby Dall of Poison are seen here at SiriusXM Studios on Dec. 4, 2019, in Los Angeles. (Emma McIntyre/Getty Images for SiriusXM)

"Even with all the treatment, it still didn't work," he recalled. "So then I got on an experimental drug combination at UC San Diego Moores Cancer Center, and it worked incredibly well. It's one of those things where, if it works, it's amazing. If it doesn't, you kind of go, 'Wow, maybe I wasted my time.' So I had to roll the dice. And I did. And when I rolled it, thankfully, it came out in my favor."

According to UC San Diego Health, Rockett participated in a clinical trial involving a combination of two drugs: pembrolizumab (Keytruda) and epacadostat. Rockett was declared free of throat cancer in July 2016.
Rikki Rockett of Poison performs onstage during The Stadium Tour at Truist Park in Atlanta, on June 16, 2022. (Getty Images for Live Nation)
The treatment took a toll. At one point, Rockett's tongue swelled so much that he feared he might choke. Soon, however, a scan offered hope.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Rikki Rockett is seen here during his cancer fight. (Courtesy of Rikki Rockett)

"The crazy thing was that my first PET scan showed that 90 percent of the cancer was already gone," Rockett wrote. "And by the second PET scan, it was all gone. It was as if the angels had come down and blessed me. I mean, it was unbelievable."
Members of Poison — Bret Michaels, C.C. DeVille, Rikki Rockett and Bobby Dall — pose on the red carpet at the 1987 MTV Music Video Awards in Universal City, California. (Getty Images)
Rockett wrote that his doctor seemed just as surprised by the results but explained that treatment needed to continue to reduce the risk of the cancer returning.
But Rockett's health challenges were far from over.
Rikki Rocket attends the Frankie Banali of Quiet Riot bronze statue unveiling and memorial at Rainbow Bar & Grill on Nov. 14, 2021, in Los Angeles. (Getty Images)
"Some eight months into the process, nothing was coming up, but I was getting high white blood cell counts," Rockett wrote.

"So, they got concerned about that, and to cut a long story short, I wound up with something called CML, chronic myeloid leukemia, and it’s a predisposition thing. It’s a translocation between BCR-ABL, the chromosomes. You’re prone to it if, like me, you have the Philadelphia chromosome. Of course, it absolutely freaked me out. I mean, I just went through one cancer, and now I was facing another one."
Rikki Rockett told Fox News Digital he's been cancer-free for 10 years. (WireImage)
Chronic myeloid leukemia is a type of blood cancer often associated with an acquired genetic abnormality known as the Philadelphia chromosome.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
American glam rock band Poison, including Bret Michaels, Rikki Rockett, C.C. DeVille and Bobby Dall, performs at Joe Louis Arena in Detroit, on Jan. 9, 1987. (Getty Images)

"The hematologist, however, took everything in stride, and when we met, she was super calm," he wrote. "She told me, ‘You picked the best leukemia you could. It’s very treatable, and sometimes curable.’ Dr. Jaimeson would be my doctor for the very long foreseeable future, and I was blessed to have her."
Rikki Rockett of Poison performs at Five Points Amphitheatre in Irvine, California, on May 18, 2018. (Getty Images)

"So, all that happened was that she put me on new medication, which I’m still on. It has some nasty side effects, but the best side effect is that CML has been 100 percent in remission! Zero detection for a number of years now! There must be a reason why I’m still here, I think to this day."
Looking back, Rockett told Fox News Digital his medical team "actually saved my life."
Rikki Rockett of Poison is seen here at the Anaheim Convention Center in Anaheim, California, on Jan. 22, 2026. (Getty Images)

Rockett still lives with the lasting effects of his treatment. But a decade after his throat cancer battle, he's focused less on what the disease took from him and more on what he lived to see — his children growing up.
"Sometimes my voice gets rough, or I get dry," he said. "I get very dry because my salivary glands got toasted with the radiation. But I’m cancer-free, and I’ve been cancer free for 10 years."
Drummer Rikki Rockett attends the 2013 NAMM Show at the Anaheim Convention Center on Jan. 24, 2013. (Getty Images for NAMM)
Rockett has no plans to slow down. He's been keeping busy performing with his band, Rockett Mafia.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Rikki Rockett hopes his memoir will encourage readers not to give up. (Courtesy of Rikki Rockett)

"I’m not out of gas yet," he said with a smile. "I still got stuff to do. And I love playing because I want my kids to see me, and they have. They’ve been to some Poison concerts. I wanted them to see me, and they did. I got that wish."
For Rockett, beating cancer meant getting the time he once feared he wouldn’t have. And he's not wasting a single second, he insisted.
Rikki Rockett is seen here with his daughter. (Instagram.com/rikkirockett)
"A big part of it was fighting for my kids," he reflected. "There’s no question that was a big chunk of my fight."
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: William Shatner finds answer to 'What the f--- is heavy metal?' after forming new band at 95
summary: William Shatner, 95, reveals his upcoming heavy metal album "What the F is Heavy Metal" features Queen's Brian May and over 50 musicians joining the project.
story: "Star Trek" icon William Shatner explains how Cleopatra Records inspired his heavy-metal project, which features more than 50 musicians, including Brian May, and led to the formation of his band, The *uckers.
William Shatner is showing no signs of slowing down as he prepares to front a heavy metal band at age 95.

In addition to his decades-long career as an actor, Shatner is also an accomplished musician, who has released 11 studio albums encompassing a wide range of genres including spoken word, rock, progressive rock, Christmas and country releases.

During an interview with Fox News Digital, Shatner, who recently partnered with over-the-counter hearing aid maker Audien Hearing for a new campaign, shared his reaction when his music label Cleopatra Records first approached him earlier this year about making a heavy metal album.
WILLIAM SHATNER SAYS HE'S 'TAKING CARE OF BUSINESS' AT 95: 'THE LEAST OF ALL I WANT DO IS DIE'
"I said, ‘What the f--- is heavy metal?’" the "Star Trek" icon recalled.
William Shatner explained why he decided to launch a heavy metal band at age 95.  (WireImage)
"And that's the title of the album, ‘What the F is Heavy Metal,’" Shatner added.
COUNTRY MUSIC SINGER SHANE SMITH PUTS HIS OWN SPIN ON JOHNNY CASH'S ICONIC 'HURT' COVER

Shatner told Fox News Digital that he teamed up with his longtime creative collaborator and friend, author Robert Sharenow, for the project. The two previously worked together on five albums featuring autobiographical lyrics and spoken-word performances.
"So we wrote six songs for the album," Shatner said. "And I laid down my track."
WATCH: WILLIAM SHATNER, 95, ANSWERS ‘WHAT THE F--- IS HEAVY METAL?' WITH NEW ALBUM
In addition to six original songs, Shatner said that "What the F is Heavy Metal" will feature covers with contributions from more than 50 musicians,

"We've got one number in the album that's gonna be out in the wintertime called ‘What the F is Heavy Metal,’" Shatner said. "All of a sudden, 50, I'm told 50 heavy metal musicians all volunteer to be on this album."
PAUL MCCARTNEY REVEALS HOW A 'HAPPY' TEEN HITCHHIKING TRIP WITH GEORGE HARRISON DELIVERED A SHOCK

The musicians included Queen's Brian May, who performed a guitar solo for one of the album's tracks titled "Rage." Shatner explained that "Rage" features the famous line "Rage, rage against the dying of the light" from the 1951 poem "Do not go gentle into that good night," written by Welsh poet Dylan Thomas.
Marcus Nand and Britt Lightning of The *uckers perform with William Shatner during Riot Fest at Douglass Park in Chicago, Ill., on Sept. 20, 2026. (WireImage)

While speaking with Fox News Digital, Shatner recalled that he was later invited to perform at Riot Fest, an annual three-day punk rock music festival held at Douglass Park in Chicago, Illinois. In a July social media post, the organizers of Riot Fest announced that Shatner would debut his heavy metal band The *uckers at the festival, noting that they had tried to book him for over a decade.
ROD STEWART CONFIRMS FINAL TOUR AFTER HEART PROCEDURE AND HEALTH SCARES

The "Boston Legal" alum said that his label tapped five musicians to form his new heavy metal band. The all-star rock and heavy metal lineup includes guitarists Marcus Nand and Britt Lightning, bassist Phil Soussan and drummer Fred Aching.
"They put together a group of fabulous musicians," Shatner said. "We call ourselves The *uckers for, you know, ‘What the f--- is heavy metal.’'"
BRET MICHAELS CANCELS REMAINING 2026 TOUR DATES HOURS AFTER 'COMEBACK' PERFORMANCE DUE TO HEALTH SCARE
Shatner's upcoming album will feature 50 heavy metal musicians.  (WireImage)

The band made its live debut in Chicago on Sept. 19 and performed at Riot Fest the following day. The *uckers played original songs including "Rage," "Sky" and "One Fear" alongside covers of Ozzy Osbourne's "Crazy Train," Motörhead's "Ace of Spades," and Metallica's "Enter Sandman."
"We went to Riot Fest … and was a huge success, huge," Shatner recalled. "They were cheering and the reviews and the people…so it proved to me the viability of ‘What the F is Heavy Metal.'"
‘A MAN WITHOUT LOVE’ SINGER ENGELBERT HUMPERDINCK CREDITS UNDERWATER WORKOUT FOR KEEPING HIM ‘ALIVE’ AT 90
After performing with The *uckers and making his heavy metal album, Shatner said he has an answer to his original question.
"It is the beat of life," he said. "It is such an energetic way of doing music. It enlivens your life. It stirs you up. It makes you pay attention."
WATCH: WILLIAM SHATNER SAYS HEAVY METAL ‘ENLIVENS’ HIS LIFE AS HE FRONTS BAND AT 95

Shatner explained that his approach to heavy metal extends beyond the music itself. For the album, he said he incorporated fresh takes on the lyrics of several classic songs, including Metallica’s "Enter Sandman," which he believes contains darker themes beneath its familiar melody.
"I've reinterpreted even the cover songs," he said.
Shatner said his version of "Enter Sandman" focuses on the sinister implications of the song’s lyrics rather than treating the Sandman as a harmless bedtime figure.
"It's a total reinterpretation of the Sandman," he said. "It is amazing."
Shatner and The *uckers performed for the first time in Chicago in September. (WireImage)

While Shatner is embracing the volume of heavy metal, the project also connects to a more personal issue. The actor is partnering with Audien Hearing on a campaign about hearing health after experiencing tinnitus and hearing loss himself.

Shatner recalled that his hearing challenges began decades ago on the set of "Star Trek." During the filming of an explosion scene featuring him alongside his co-star Leonard Nimoy, the stage doors were accidentally left closed, preventing the blast from dissipating properly.

He told Fox News Digital that the two actors were taken to a doctor after their ears began ringing. Shatner said that he did not immediately realize that the noise had become permanent. The Canada native recalled that while walking on the beach one day, he noticed that the hiss of the retreating waves never completely disappeared.
"I heard the hiss, but the hiss never went away," he said. "It was always hissing."
The actor said the album features reinterpreted versions of hit heavy metal songs.  (Getty Images)

Shatner said he eventually learned to live with the tinnitus through a process known as habituation. He also estimated that he has lost roughly 20% to 30% of his hearing and said hearing aids have helped him rediscover everyday sounds.
"The dog claws on the floor, the creak of this rocking chair — all the panoply of sounds that go to make up the richness of the world around us, we’re using hearing," he said.
Shatner's hearing challenges have not stopped him from playing heavy metal. However, he said the loud music can temporarily intensify the tinnitus, which he noticed after performing at Riot Fest.
"Now I'm fitted with earphones, right? And the sound would have been blasting in anyway, but it's heavy metal sound," he said. "I'm blasting in on my tinnitus."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
"So there is this noise," Shatner continued. "Either I'm going to perform with the noise or I'm not going to perform."
"And my tinnitus is just coming back down now," he added. "It was hissing so loudly being subjected to that sound."
WATCH: WILLIAM SHATNER SAYS HE PERFORMED THROUGH ‘LOUD’ TINNITUS DURING HEAVY-METAL DEBUT AT 95

Despite the challenges that come with performing through tinnitus, Shatner said he is moving ahead with the album. He told Fox News Digital that the tracks have already been recorded, but he plans to listen to the completed music and determine whether he needs to make any changes to his performance.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"In effect, the album has been made, but I'm going in a week or two to listen to it to see how much of an adjustment in my performance I need to do with these musicians, who are playing in an area that I really don't know," he said.
Shatner said the first single from the upcoming album will be released this winter.  (WireImage)
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
"I want to see if my performance needs to be adjusted to their tempo and their meaning of the heavy metal," Shatner continued. "So that's what's going to happen."

"This is going to be a major thing in heavy metal," he added. "'What the F Is Heavy Metal,'" with 50 of the greatest people, including Brian May, on the album."

title: Sylvester Stallone scoffs at nepotism critics over daughter's 'Tulsa King' role: 'You idiot'
summary: Sylvester Stallone fires back at nepotism critics over casting daughter Scarlet Rose Stallone in "Tulsa King" with a blunt parenting defense.
story: Stallone reflects on the toll of decades in action movies, citing nine back operations, three neck fusions and other injuries. He says performers should leave stunts to the professionals.
Sylvester Stallone isn't apologizing for giving his daughter a shot in Hollywood.

The 80-year-old action star is pushing back against criticism of nepotism after casting his daughter, Scarlet Rose Stallone, in his crime drama "Tulsa King," delivering a blunt response to those who question whether she earned her place on the show.

"First, they go, 'Nepotism is terrible.' I said, 'Oh please, you're not a good parent if you haven't performed a little nepotism. Then obviously you don't care about your kids, because they come first,'" he said, according to USA Today.

title: Engelbert Humperdinck says he tied up a nurse during tuberculosis sanatorium stay after painful treatment
summary: Engelbert Humperdinck revealed on his podcast how he tied up a nurse during his 1961 tuberculosis sanatorium stay after painful daily injections.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Engelbert Humperdinck opened up about the time he spent in a sanatorium in 1961.

During a recent episode of his podcast, "The Engelbert Humperdinck Show," the 90-year-old British singer recalled his time at Leicester's Groby Road Hospital Sanatorium, after he was diagnosed with tuberculosis.

When speaking about the treatments he endured, he described having "to stay on your back for I don't know 8 weeks," without attempting to sit up or "do anything strenuous," in addition to getting "an injection with a needle about this big in your butt" every morning.

"There was one lady nurse who was, I don't think she liked me very much because of the injection that she gave me, she really hurt, and I used to scream at her and I used to ask for somebody else. They wouldn't give me anybody else, but this lady was very bad, and she was really hurt, and I had big blue marks," he explained.
Humperdinck rebelled against a nurse administering his injections during his time at a sanatorium. (Steve Parsons-WPA Pool/Getty Images)
ENGELBERT HUMPERDINCK SAYS HE ‘WENT THROUGH HELL’ REJECTING 'CASTING COUCH' ADVANCES EARLY IN CAREER
After she continued to hurt him with every injection, Humperdinck thought to himself, "When I'm a little better I'm going to do something" and be a bit "mischievous" to get back at her.

"I said to my friend in the next bed, I said, 'I've got to get some rope. I get some rope,'" he said. "So we got this rope, and when the nurse came around in the morning before doctor's rounds, I got the nurse, grabbed her, tied her hands behind the back, put her in the empty bed next to us, covered her up."
He said when the doctor came by for his rounds, "he knew that I was responsible for that..but he ignored it" and "just walked straight by."
Once she was free from the bindings, the singer said he "was in trouble," but that he "never let her give me another injection."
Humperdinck spent six months in a sanatorium in 1961, after being diagnosed with tuberculosis. (Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)

"I said, 'I don't want her to give me,'" he said. "And they had a male nurse come and do it for me, and it was much better."

Humperdinck spent six months in the sanatorium after he started coughing up blood during a concert in Manchester. After initially receiving a diagnosis of "a bad throat infection," his mom told the doctor 'I'm not happy with that. Not when I see blood,' and demanded an X-ray.
He explained that within an hour of getting the X-ray he was told to pack his belongings as he had tuberculosis and needed to be sent to the sanatorium.

"Eight weeks later, when I became negative from this disease, my mother visited and, I said, 'Mom, is this place a great place?' I said, 'Cause you remember when you brought me in, the priest was here spent an hour with me,'" he said. "She said, 'Son he was giving you the last rites.' Apparently I had three days."

Robert Kelker-Kelly, the actor best known for playing Bo Brady on "Days of Our Lives," experienced chest and arm pain shortly before his death at 62, according to a police report detailing his final hours.

The St. Peters Police Department report, obtained by Fox News Digital, stated that Kelker-Kelly's wife, Allison Kelly, told police she picked up her husband, who also worked as a professional pilot, from Spirit of St. Louis Airport at approximately 7:30pm on Oct. 3.
During the drive home, Kelker-Kelly said he felt pain in his left arm and chest and asked his wife to pull over so he could vomit, according to the report.

After arriving at their Missouri residence, Kelker-Kelly changed his clothes and got into bed. He continued experiencing pain and asked his wife to get him an aspirin, according to the report.
When Kelly returned from the kitchen, she found her husband unresponsive and not breathing.
She called 911 and began performing CPR, according to the report.

title: John Goodman admits he felt 'frightened' after the  sudden fame he experienced from 'Roseanne'
summary: John Goodman admitted he was his "own worst enemy" when fame hit after "Roseanne," sharing how the shift from actor to celebrity shook him deeply.
story: Roseanne Barr told Fox News Digital that living in Texas has been a "dream come true."
John Goodman is getting real about the downside of starring in one of the biggest sitcoms of all time.
During a conversation with the SAG-AFTRA Foundation, the 74-year-old actor admitted he was "frightened" by the level of fame he achieved following his starring role in "Roseanne" and other projects.
When asked what his biggest pitfalls were that he wished he would have foreseen, he replied he wished he would have understood fame better.
"I wish I would have taken to it better," he said. "I didn't. I was frightened … I'm my own worst enemy, by far."
Goodman shared he didn't take to fame very well. (Steve Granitz/FilmMagic)
ROSEANNE BARR HASN’T SPOKEN TO TV SISTER LAURIE METCALF SINCE SHOW’S CANCELLATION

Earlier in the conversation with interviewer Joe Neumaier, Goodman was asked about the way his career picked up in the late ‘80s and early '90s, and how he shifted from being a more independent actor to being a celebrity.

"It changed ,'" he said. "That's when I was told, ‘You better get a publicist and get a hold of this stuff.’ And I just … I had a bad time dealing with how famous I got all of a sudden, and just [said], ‘Well, that ain’t me.'"

He added, "It took a long time to deal with it, so I got that out of the way. But just the negotiations you have to go through, the things you have to do to sell a film, they're not ideal, but they need to be done. People put a lot of money into these things, and let's help each other out and get this done. They have a job to do, and you have to support it."
Goodman said he had a "bad time" when he achieved fame so quickly after "Roseanne." (Getty Images)

At another point in the interview, Goodman shared he agreed to do "Roseanne" "to quit living out of a suitcase," adding that he "hit it off with [Roseanne Barr] immediately, to the point where, and not in an arrogant way, I just knew when I left that I had the job."
"Roseanne" aired on ABC for nine seasons from 1988 to 1997, releasing 222 episodes in its first run and winning four Emmy Awards.

"At the time, the hot shows in television were all wealth porn, like 'Dynasty,' 'Dallas,' stuff like that. And we were sober reality," he said. "Rose said something early on that 'just because we're poor doesn't make us stupid.' And the reason that family stayed together was because of laughter and obvious love. And I think that showed on the screen in a real way."

Following his time on "Roseanne," Goodman starred in many successful movies, including "The Flintstones," "The Big Lebowski," "Monsters Inc." and others, before returning to the role of Dan Conner in the "Roseanne" reboot in 2018.

Just a few weeks later, ABC announced that the show's cast would be returning for a new spin-off, "The Conners," without Barr. The show aired for 112 episodes from 2018 to 2025, with Goodman filming that and "The Righteous Gemstones" at the same time.

"I didn’t think [the 'Roseanne' reboot] was going to go beyond the initial five or six episodes. I thought it’d be a one-off thing, and then we got picked up, and Roseanne got fired," he told The Hollywood Reporter in July 2025. title: ‘Little House on the Prairie’ star says brutal filming conditions left cast members unconscious
summary: Alison Arngrim revealed she passed out on her first day filming "Little House on the Prairie" in Simi Valley, and Sean Penn also fainted on set.
story: Sidney Greenbush recalls behind-the-scenes memories with the ‘Little House on the Prairie’ cast and explains why she stepped away from acting. Greenbush is the author of a new children's book, ‘Seven Sisters – The Lantern of Humanity.’
The cast of "Little House on the Prairie" is opening up about the brutal reality of filming the hit TV series.
Cast members were guests on Patrick Labyorteaux's podcast to discuss their experiences on the show. He asked Alison Arngrim, who starred as Nellie Oleson, what the first day was like for her.
"Complete chaos and confusion," Arngrim admitted.
‘LITTLE HOUSE ON THE PRAIRIE’ STAR SAYS CHILD ACTORS GET ‘DROPPED’ AFTER HOLLYWOOD FAME FADES
Alison Arngrim and other "Little House on the Prairie" cast members spoke about their experiences filming the show. (NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty Images)
She explained that she hadn't known she was supposed to show up with her character's signature ringlet curls,
"So, it was lots of panic and phone calls back and forth, and then massive curling of my hair. So, yeah, bananas. And then, first day on location, of course, I pass out.
"So, I was off to just a rousing start right there."
The conversation also included fellow cast members Dean Butler, Pamela Roylance and Jennifer Donati, as well as Tracy and Victor French, the children of late cast member Victor French.
Labyorteaux also starred in "Little House on the Prairie" as Andy Garvey.

During a later conversation about how hot it was in Simi Valley, where the show was filmed, Arngrim joked that the cast and crew were able to tell when summer hit because the "first day of summer is when Alison hits the ground because I was out like that. It was that hot."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Michael Landon directs Melissa Gilbert and Melissa Sue Anderson in an episode of "Little House on the Prairie." (NBCU Photo Bank)

Speaking again of her first day on set, she explained she was "so disciplined," she approached the director and said, "Excuse me, I think I'm going to faint" before she "completely lost consciousness and dropped."

"It's, like, basically how to not pass out was the challenge," she continued. "It was insane, though the great thing is that other people began to pass out, so people realized it wasn't me, the first one being Sean Penn."
Penn, who was a child at the time, "didn't wake up and come back to work. That was it. He was done for the day."

Arngrim said, "That's when they decided maybe it was not just me, that it was actually that hot."

Later in the podcast, the subject of their least favorite episodes came up, and Arngrim shared that she disliked any episodes where sporting events were involved because that meant sitting in bleachers "where it was 100 million degrees" for hours at a time while crew members filmed reaction shots.
Several cast members of the show agreed that filming in Simi Valley was brutally hot. (NBCU Photo Bank)

She recalled one of these shoots when Charlotte Stewart, who played school teacher Eva Beadle Simms, "was just sitting there, and she had, in fact, lost consciousness and fainted and blacked out, but just didn't fall over, and they didn't know she was out."

Of the sweltering set, Butler admitted, "You just had to do whatever strategy you could. I always felt sorry for the women on the set. … [The men] were basically dressed in a shirt and pants and dog-eared boots" while the female cast members wore dresses, petticoats, stockings and sometimes wigs.

Roylance shared that Michael Landon, who acted as executive producer, writer and director on "Little House" in addition to his starring role, let her film one scene with her blouse unbuttoned and her sleeves rolled up because "it was just miserable hot" that day on the set.
Roylance said that Stan Ivar, who played her character's husband, gave her a fan that she could wear under her costume when she wasn't filming. (NBCUniversal via Getty Images)
"It kind of just wasn't done," she said of the way she wore the blouse, "but it's in the shot. You can see it in the episode, and I was so grateful for that."

Donati, who, along with her twin sister, was an infant when she played Baby Rose Wilder, joked, "I don't want to brag, but I think I was the most pampered cast member there. They didn't let me get hot."

The cast of "Little House on the Prairie" included Matthew Laborteaux as Albert Quinn Ingalls, Melissa Gilbert as Laura Elizabeth Ingalls Wilder, Michael Landon as Charles Philip Ingalls, Dean Butler as Almanzo James Wilder, Melissa Sue Anderson as Mary Ingalls Kendall, Linwood Boomer as Adam Kendall, Karen Grassle as Caroline Quiner Holbrook Ingalls and one of the Greenbush sisters as Carrie Ingalls. "Little House on the Prairie" was a Western family drama loosely based on Laura Ingalls Wilder's semi-autobiographical books. It follows the Ingalls family as it builds a life in Walnut Grove, Minnesota, during the late 19th century.

Landon starred as the Ingalls family patriarch, Charles. Karen Grassle played his wife, Caroline, and Gilbert portrayed their daughter, Laura. The series premiered on NBC in 1974 and ran for nine seasons, through 1983, followed by three television movies.

title: 'Virgin River' star Ben Hollingsworth says his kids have freedom in small town that 'doesn't fly' in LA
summary: Ben Hollingsworth says filming "Virgin River" led his family to leave LA for a small town, giving his kids outdoor freedoms he had growing up.
story: The actor told Fox News Digital that living outside Los Angeles allows his children the opportunity to freely play outside like he was able to do as a kid.
Ben Hollingsworth is all about giving his young kids the freedoms he grew up with.

During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 42-year-old actor discussed his participation in the upcoming Meet Cute Con, the latest season of "Virgin River" and how raising his kids in a small town affords them certain freedoms.

"Our kids are actually, we're able to kind of let them go off and be, like, be back at five, which I feel like is kind of gone away now," he explained. "It's really, really tricky to do that. You definitely can't do it in major cities, or you'll be arrested as a parent. Like, what are you doing? Letting your kid run across Ventura Boulevard? In LA, that doesn't fly."

He said he's "thankful" he is able to give his children the kind of life where they can play outside as long as they are "back by this time when the sun goes down," noting, "I'm happy to provide them with some of what I got growing up."
Hollingsworth shared he is giving his kids the freedoms he had when he was growing up. (Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images for IMDb)
'DESPERATE HOUSEWIVES' STAR JAMES DENTON SAYS LA IS 'NOT A GREAT PLACE TO RAISE KIDS' DUE TO IMAGE CULTURE
Another way they have managed to keep their children out of the Hollywood bubble and grounded is by keeping them active in sports and through family activities, including hikes.
WATCH: Ben Hollingsworth is 'grateful' to give his three children the childhood he had
The actor also shared that while shooting Season 3 of the show in British Columbia, Canada, his wife got pregnant with their third child and inspired their big life change.
WATCH: Ben Hollingsworth and his family moved to a 'Virgin River-esque town'
"I'll be transparent with you. I won't say where we are, but we did move out of a large center, and we actually did move to a very Virgin River-esque town because of 'Virgin River,'" he said.

"We got pregnant with our third, and we made a decision to put down roots in a smaller place. And raising your kids in a small town is just, it's a luxury, and we're very happy that we're able to provide that for the kiddos."

He admitted that, for them, spending more time outside of Los Angeles happened "organically," noting that he isn't the only Hollywood star choosing to leave the city, citing Jana Kramer and Bethany Joy Lenz as examples.
Hollingsworth and his wife decided to move to a small town while expecting their third child. (Tibrina Hobson/Getty Images for Karen Kingsbury's Productions)
JONAH HILL ABANDONED LOS ANGELES TO RAISE GROWING FAMILY IN ‘VERY SMALL TOWN’
Hollingsworth also shared his excitement about participating in the upcoming Meet Cute Con at the Loveless Barn and Virgin Hotels Nashville between Nov. 6-8.

The "Small Town Swoon" themed event will bring together stars from "Virgin River," "One Tree Hill" and "The Way Home," providing fans with the warmth, romance and community they see on television in real-life.
WATCH: Ben Hollingsworth says 'Virgin River' is 'apple pie entertainment'

"I think community is the key," he said. "In today's world, we're losing that sense of community more and more every day, I feel like. And there's something really great about getting together and bringing a fan community together with some of the people that they're excited about, and they're used to seeing on the screen. They can meet and see in real life and ask questions that they've been dying to ask."
He is looking forward to meeting fans, noting it's the first time the entire cast of "Virgin River" has "gotten together as a cast to do this in the public," saying it "just felt right."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Hollingsworth is excited to meet the fans of "Virgin River" at Meet Cute Con. (Roy Rochlin/Getty Images for Netflix)
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"It felt really great. We love Nashville. Who doesn't love Nashville? They're doing it at this barn, and it's not gonna be this massive convention center," he added. "It's a small, intimate thing. So, everyone who comes is gonna be a few feet away from us. And that really kind of helped sell it to us that we should do one."
When it comes to the success of his own show, Hollingsworth cited the idea that it speaks to "a part of America that that we don't celebrate enough."

He explained that many television shows on Netflix and other streaming services tell stories of people in big cities, but as "more and more communities outside those centers have gained access" to these services, stories with "small town charm" and a "sense of community" have begun to resonate.

"We really took off during the pandemic," he said. "Because I think just … that it was a comforting show, it is a comforting show. We really take pride in kind of supplying — it's almost like medicine for people. You don't need to take whatever to go to sleep. You can watch a nice episode of 'Virgin River' and it's like a warm fuzzy blanket, or a hug.

title: Jessie James Decker used kitchen secret to win over NFL star husband in one weekend
summary: Jessie James Decker reveals how she made husband Eric Decker fall in love with her in one weekend. Her "The Secret Sauce" cookbook is out now.
story: ‘The Secret Sauce’ author and country singer tells Fox News Digital how she ‘sealed the deal’ with husband and former NFL star Eric Decker through her cooking and shares the secret to their marriage.
Jessie James Decker knows the way to her man's heart, and it involves a little spice.
The country singer revealed how she won over her husband, Eric Decker, after just one weekend together.
"I mean, we all know he loves the jambalaya. That's how I sealed the deal and had him fall in love with me after one weekend," Jessie, co-author of "The Secret Sauce," told Fox News Digital.
JESSIE JAMES DECKER RAISES ATHLETIC KIDS "BAREFOOT AND BEING FREE" INSTEAD OF GLUED TO IPADS
Jessie James Decker said she won over husband Eric Decker with this spicy secret after just one weekend together. (JC Olivera/Variety via Getty Images)

More than 13 years into their marriage, the former NFL wide receiver is still one of Jessie's biggest fans in the kitchen, although the singer admits that food isn't just fuel in the Decker household. It's practically a love language.

"I couldn't have married someone that didn't just enjoy food," Jessie emphasized. "And there's people out there that are like that. They're just like a meal's a meal. I'm like, it is an event. It's a celebration. Everything is."
Country singer Jessie James Decker said food is a love language in her household, where husband Eric Decker has developed a taste for her Southern and Cajun cooking. (Getty Images)
When Jessie and Eric met, the country singer said he was "a Midwestern guy" who had never had Southern Cajun food.
Now, the "Cajun Queen" chapter of her new cookbook, "The Secret Sauce," which she wrote with her mother and sister, has earned a special place on his plate.

Jessie James Decker is sharing her love of cooking and treasured family traditions in her fourth cookbook, "The Secret Sauce." (Diana King)

Jessie James Decker said sitting down for dinner with husband Eric Decker and their four children is one family tradition she refuses to sacrifice despite their busy schedules. (Instagram/Jessie James Decker)

title: Kelly Clarkson risks looking like 'rich and famous prima donna' in $15K bird fight, expert says
summary: Crisis PR experts weigh in on whether Kelly Clarkson's dispute with Brooklyn boutique Art of Play over a $15,000 mechanical bird hurts her image.
story: Fox News host Will Cain discusses singer Kelly Clarkson's social media post about her feud with a toy store in Brooklyn, N.Y., on 'The Will Cain Show.'
Kelly Clarkson’s public dispute with a Brooklyn small business over a $15,000 mechanical bird could damage the relatable image she has built over the past two decades, a crisis PR expert warned.

"There will certainly be some naysayers who think Clarkson was acting like a rich and famous prima donna and using her platform vindictively," Steve Honig, founder of The Honig Company, told Fox News Digital.
"But most people will likely think that, for the most part, she acted accordingly and in many ways was a role model for standing up for oneself."
The controversy began after Clarkson claimed she was treated like Julia Roberts’ character in "Pretty Woman" while shopping at Art of Play in Brooklyn.
KELLY CLARKSON'S STORE CALLOUT SHOWS THE 'POWER' OF CELEBRITY STATEMENTS: EXPERT
Kelly Clarkson sparked a public feud with a Brooklyn boutique store over a sales dispute.  (GC Images)

Clarkson said an employee appeared to judge her based on her appearance and suggested she look at "something comparable" instead of the $15,000 mechanical bird she wanted to purchase. She also called the employee an "idiot" and said the store lost a major sale.

Art of Play, which sells puzzles, games, toys, books and other specialty items, responded to Clarkson's original social media post, saying the business had been bombarded with hateful messages from "8 million people" after the singer's accusations.

"Imagine our surprise when our small local business was suddenly attacked by 8 million people who have never visited our store. It’s been a surreal experience to be the focus of such widespread outrage after just one mention by a celebrity," the store wrote on its Instagram page Sunday afternoon.

"Thanks to all our friends for their support and welcome to all the curious folks who discovered us amidst the drama. We’re going to keep our heads down and hopefully, we can clear things up with Kelly someday. As a talented popular singer once said ‘what doesn’t kill you makes you stronger.'"
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
After Art of Play's Instagram post, Clarkson responded Sunday afternoon on X and Instagram stories to the store's assertion that the mechanical bird wasn't for sale.
"Cool, cool. Sure, it wasn't for sale. That's the narrative Art of Play is gonna go with," Clarkson wrote, adding a thumbs-up emoji.

"So the whole conversation we had when I asked you if it was for sale whilst pointing to the price tag hanging on the wall with the title Singing Bird didn't happen as you elevator eyed me saying in a condescending tone "yes, it’s for sale but it costs 15,000 dollars so if you’d like me to find something comparable for you I can." That all never happened and now it’s not for sale. Okay, cool. So you’re not only rude, you’re also a liar. Got it.
Kelly Clarkson likened a recent shopping experience to Julia Roberts' character in "Pretty Woman." (Getty Images)

"And by the way, I obviously support small businesses because I was literally at a small business trying to purchase things. I love small businesses and know they are important and I always support them, but you don’t get a free pass to treat people less than in your store just because you are a small business. It’s not that hard to be kind. I never blast people but you my friend were an exception. Your store is really cool. Unfortunately, you aren’t."

Clarkson’s post also prompted criticism online, with some users accusing her of using her platform to target a small business. The store reportedly received a wave of negative Google reviews after the singer’s comments went viral.
SELMA BLAIR SAYS 'NO ONE RETURNED MY CALLS' AFTER ANTI-ISLAM COMMENT LED TO HOLLYWOOD FALLOUT
Art of Play shared another post on Instagram Sunday to "clarify one additional detail" about Clarkson's visit.

"During the 5 minutes she spent in the store, she inquired about our mechanical bird puppet named Molly. We explained that while Molly is permanently attached to the wall and serves as a de facto mascot for our shop, a nearly identical automaton is owned by the creator of the machines, a brilliant artist named Bliss Kolb who lives in Seattle. He told us he would be willing to part with Molly’s twin for $15,000. We explained all of this to Kelly Clarkson.
Kelly Clarkson won the first season of "American Idol" in 2002. (Kevin Winter/ImageDirect)

"We also offered to show her a different singing bird automaton, made by a traditional clockmaking shop in Germany, that she could have taken home with her that day. It costs about $2,000. She did not stick around long enough to see it.
"We’ve reached out to Kelly directly to try and clear the air," the shop concluded. "We really do wish her the best and hope that someday we can all laugh about this misunderstanding."

Adam Rubin, co-owner of Art of Play and a children’s author, spoke with Fox News Digital inside the Brooklyn store Tuesday morning, claiming the singer has put his business in danger after their viral dispute.
Rubin claimed the backlash has extended beyond angry comments online, with people associated with the business allegedly facing threats and having their personal information exposed.
"We've got incredible support from our neighbors and fans over the past few days, and all of them have been attacked, threatened, doxed," he said.
Molly, a mechanical singing bird designed by Bliss Kolb, is displayed at Art of Play in Brooklyn. The price tag now reads $15 million. (Fox News Digital)

Evan Nierman, CEO of crisis PR firm Red Banyan, said Clarkson’s long-established reputation will likely protect her from any lasting damage but warned that continuing to discuss the dispute could change how some people view her.
"Arguing with a boutique toy store over a $15,000 mechanical bird is not going to make or break the long-term reputation of a literal ‘American Idol,’" Nierman said.
"Right or wrong, she initiated this conflict by telling her 9 million followers that the owners of the store are idiots who lost a huge sale and mistreated her.
TAYLOR HICKS CREDITS FAITH AND BLUE-COLLAR BIRMINGHAM ROOTS FOR KEEPING HIM GROUNDED AFTER 'AMERICAN IDOL' WIN
"Prior to this incident, she was perceived as a down-to-earth and relatable celebrity, but this acrimonious back and forth over social media is sullying everyone involved."
The co-owner of Art and Play told Fox News Digital, "I am afraid for the safety of our shop. Kelly Clarkson has put us in danger." (Denise Truscello/Getty Images for Live Nation Las Vegas)
Honig argued that the dispute could ultimately strengthen Clarkson’s image because she presented herself as someone standing up to unfair treatment.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"The dispute is more likely to strengthen Clarkson’s image than undermine it because she was standing up against being judged based on appearance," Honig said. "This was not really about a $15,000 item, but about how she says she was treated when she tried to buy it.
"Just as in ‘Pretty Woman,’ someone appeared to be judging a book by its cover."
Still, Honig acknowledged that the situation could become more damaging if the dispute continues.

"There will certainly be some naysayers who think Clarkson was acting like a rich and famous prima donna and using her platform vindictively," Steve Honig told Fox News Digital.   (Matthew Stockman/Getty Images)
"The only risk is if the dispute drags on and starts to look like a celebrity using her platform against a small business," he said.
Nierman also urged Clarkson to let the controversy fade rather than risk having the dispute overshadow her career.

"Clarkson has built up over two decades of goodwill since winning ‘American Idol.’ She has built a deep reservoir of trust, and her fans will give her the benefit of the doubt every time in a fight like this," he said.

"Every new round of arguing over Molly the Bird makes it more likely that the general American public will start to make conclusions about Clarkson and her character based on this dispute, which does not serve her.
Kelly Clarkson rose to fame after winning the inaugural season of "American Idol" in 2002 and has built a successful career as a singer and television host. (Art Streiber/NBC via Getty Image)

"Clarkson should do what she can to move past this, since she wants the first thing people think about her to be her musical accomplishments and not a petty and protracted fight over a singing birdie."
Honig said Clarkson should eventually "declare victory and move on," while Nierman suggested she ask her supporters to stop harassing the store.

"Kelly’s silence has been helpful and the right move," Nierman said. "But if she really wanted to win the day and come out permanently ahead, she could call on her fans to stand down and leave the store and its employees alone."
A representative for Clarkson did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Fox News Digital's Danielle Minnetian contributed to this report.

title: Judge tosses Timothy Busfield's indictment on child sex abuse charges
summary: District Court Judge Joseph Montano granted Busfield's motion to throw out the grand jury indictment on Friday. Prosecutors can refile.
story: New Mexico criminal defense attorney John W. Day told Fox News Digital Timothy Busfield will appear before a judge after turning himself in to authorities following an arrest warrant in connection with child sex abuse charges.
A New Mexico judge on Friday dismissed actor/director Timothy Busfield’s indictment on child sexual abuse charges.
District Court Judge Joseph Montano granted Busfield's motion to throw out the grand jury indictment.
Busfield had been indicted on four counts of criminal sexual contact with a minor.
TIMOTHY BUSFIELD INDICTED ON CHILD SEX ABUSE CHARGES IN NEW MEXICO

In a court filing obtained by Fox News Digital, the judge found the prosecutor "failed to act in a fair and impartial manner," including by failing "to properly instruct the grand jury on the law for calling witnesses and in instructing the grand jurors on a procedure that effectively withheld requested witnesses.

"In doing so, the grand jury proceedings were conducted in a manner that violated grand jury statutes designed to protect the structural integrity of our grand jury system, and the presumption of prejudice applies.
Timothy Busfield in a New Mexico courtroom Jan. 20, 2026. (Getty Images)
"The State, however, remains free to institute new criminal proceedings against Defendant," the filing adds.

During a September hearing, Busfield’s attorney, Amanda Fayerberg, played audio recordings of grand jurors asking to hear from additional witnesses. She said prosecutors wrongly informed jurors that subpoenas would be needed, even though those witnesses were "present, available and willing to testify."

Bernalillo County District Attorney Greer Staley countered that the defense hadn’t followed the correct process for submitting evidence to a grand jury and that Busfield improperly and "excessively" tried to steer grand jurors toward favorable witnesses and exhibits during his three-hour testimony.
"The State, however, remains free to institute new criminal proceedings against Defendant."

Nancy Laflin, communications director for the 2nd Judicial District Attorney, told Fox News Digital, "Our office has received the order and is evaluating our options to determine how we will proceed."
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Busfield has repeatedly denied the allegations against him. In an email Friday, Fayerberg told The Associated Press he was "relieved and grateful" after reading the judge’s decision.
When Busfield was indicted earlier this year, his attorney issued a statement to Fox News Digital, saying a "grand jury will indict a ham sandwich."
Busfield was indicted on four counts of criminal sexual contact with a minor. (Rodin Eckenroth/Getty Images)

"What is deeply concerning is that the district attorney is choosing to proceed on a case that is fundamentally unsound and cannot be proven at trial. The detention hearing exposed fatal weaknesses in the state’s evidence, gaps that no amount of charging decisions can cure," Larry Stein said in February.

"This prosecution appears driven by something other than the facts or the law," he added. "Mr. Busfield will fight these charges at every stage and looks forward to testing the state’s case in open court — where evidence matters — not behind closed doors."

Busfield, 68, first surrendered to local authorities on child sex abuse charges Jan. 13, days after an arrest warrant was issued for the "West Wing" actor. He was held without bail at the time of his arrest on two counts of criminal sexual contact with a minor and one count of child abuse.

Timothy Busfield's wife, Melissa Gilbert, reacts as her husband was granted a conditional release in the 2nd District Judicial Court at the Bernalillo County Courthouse in Albuquerque, N.M., Jan. 20, 2026. (AJ Skuy for Fox News Digital)
He denied the claims upon surrendering and is "determined to clear his name," according to a statement from Stein provided to Fox News Digital.
